content:
Wen Jiabao, Jia Qinglin and others attended the conference

A ceremony commemorating the 100th anniversary of Jiang Zemin's birth was held at the Great Hall of the People in Beijing on the morning of Monday (17th). Xi Jinping, General Secretary of the CPC Central Committee, President of the State, and Chairman of the Central Military Commission, as well as all incumbent members of the Political Bureau Standing Committee, attended. Retired leaders including Wen Jiabao, Jia Qinglin, Zhang Dejiang, Yu Zhengsheng, Li Zhanshu, Wang Yang, Li Lanqing, Zeng Qinghong, Li Changchun, He Guoqiang, Liu Yunshan, Wang Qishan, and Zhang Gaoli were also present.

Hu Jintao was not seen; Li Ruihuan, Wu Guanzheng and Luo Gan were absent

However, Hu Jintao, who succeeded Jiang Zemin as General Secretary of the CPC Central Committee, President of the State, and Chairman of the Central Military Commission, was not seen in CCTV's live broadcast. In addition, Li Ruihuan, Wu Guanzheng and Luo Gan, who had served as members of the Political Bureau Standing Committee during Jiang Zemin's time, were also absent from the ceremony.

「1989年嚴重政治風波及江澤民堅決執行黨中央決策」

In a major speech at the ceremony, Xi Jinping reviewed how Jiang Zemin went from serving as Shanghai Party Secretary to becoming the core of the third generation of the CPC's central leadership collective. In particular, he said: 「In the spring and summer of 1989, a serious political disturbance occurred in our country. Comrade Jiang Zemin firmly upheld and implemented the correct decisions of the CPC Central Committee, and effectively maintained stability in Shanghai.」

Xi Jinping also said there was a need to learn from Jiang Zemin's 「unyielding political faith」, describing how, in the face of major tests posed by the changing international situation in the late 1980s and early 1990s and the serious political disturbance that occurred in the country, he remained unwavering in adhering to the focus on economic development. He also emphasized approaches such as governing the country must first involve governing the Party, and governing the Party must be conducted strictly.

Xi Jinping also said there was a need to learn from Jiang Zemin's 「forward-looking strategic thinking」, mentioning that under Jiang Zemin's leadership, Hong Kong and Macau returned to China smoothly, and that he promoted the reaching of the 「1992 Consensus」 between the two sides of the Taiwan Strait, which embodies the one-China principle.

The focus of outside attention is on why Beijing is holding a large-scale event to commemorate the centenary of Jiang Zemin's birth at this time, and the political signals conveyed by Xi Jinping's speech.

Independent political scholar Chen Daoyin said that holding a large-scale commemorative event on the centenary of a deceased leader's birth is an institutional convention. Many important leaders in the past, such as Mao Zedong and Deng Xiaoping, have also had large-scale centenary commemorative events. As the core of the CPC's third generation of leadership, it is in line with established practice and the appropriate level for a large-scale event to be held to mark the centenary of Jiang Zemin's birth.

Scholar: references to 1989 do not amount to a new formulation

Regarding Xi's active reference to Jiang Zemin's political position in 1989 while commemorating him, Chen Daoyin believes that 1989 was an important turning point in China's politics and in Jiang Zemin's political career. Jiang Zemin had been a local leader on the verge of retirement, but because he had 「chosen the right side」 that year, he was appointed to a critical position and transferred to Beijing to replace Zhao Ziyang, becoming the core of the CPC's third generation of central leadership. Therefore, any review of his life must address the events of 1989.

Chen Daoyin said Jiang Zemin's firm maintenance of the decisions of the CPC Central Committee that year echoes Xi's current political requirement to uphold the 「Two Upholds」, making it all the more necessary to bring it up again. He also believes that Xi Jinping's remarks concerning 1989 are all definitive assessments of Jiang's legacy, and do not offer a new formulation; therefore, there is no need for outside observers to overinterpret Xi's renewed reference to 1989.

As for the large-scale commemorative event marking the centenary of Jiang Zemin's birth, Hu Jintao, the core of the CPC's fourth generation of leadership, was absent. Chen Daoyin said that although retired leaders are not necessarily required to attend such events, given that this was a major event commemorating Jiang Zemin, Hu Jintao, as his successor, would ordinarily be expected to attend. His absence could be due to factors such as not being in Beijing or being unwell. He pointed out that attention could be paid to whether Hu Jintao sent a floral tribute for Zhu Rongji's funeral on Tuesday (18th).

Zhao Jianmin, former dean of the College of Social Sciences at Chinese Culture University in Taiwan and a specialist in China's political development and cross-Strait relations, believes that Xi's speech provided a comprehensive review of Jiang Zemin's life. The key points in Jiang's political career—including putting forward the important thought of the 「Three Represents」, the reaching of the 「1992 Consensus」 across the Taiwan Strait, and firmly upholding the decisions of the CPC Central Committee in 1989—are all unavoidable subjects in any review of Jiang.

Zhao Jianmin said it was normal for Xi to focus only on Jiang's firm support for the CPC Central Committee in 1989, without making any further remarks about the June 4 incident.

Zhao Jianmin also pointed out that Xi's emphasis on the centenary of Jiang Zemin's birth has a personal dimension. He believes that Xi's later promotion—from a leader in Fujian to serving successively as the top official in Zhejiang, a major economic province, and Shanghai—laid the foundation for his entry into the top leadership, and that Jiang Zemin played an important and crucial role in this process.

He believes that Xi's emphasis on commemorating Jiang Zemin shows, on the one hand, that Xi values old ties and gratitude. On the other hand, by evaluating Jiang Zemin and emphasizing his promotion of strict Party governance and anti-corruption work, Xi can show that the relevant policies inherit and continue the direction of work from the Jiang Zemin era. This represents the implementation of an existing consensus within the Party, and can help clarify rumors circulating in public discourse.

Emphasizing the importance of obeying the CPC Central Committee at moments of major right and wrong

However, veteran China commentator Cai Shenkun has a different view. He described Xi's public reference to Jiang Zemin's position during the 1989 「political disturbance」 as unusual, and pointed out that while Jiang Zemin was alive, and even after his death, his family hoped to downplay rather than emphasize how he rose to the center of the highest levels of power as a result of the June 4 incident.

Cai Shenkun believes that Xi's special emphasis on this point was intended to highlight the importance of obeying the CPC Central Committee and maintaining political loyalty at moments involving major questions of right and wrong.

In addition, Cai Shenkun pointed out that the 21st National Congress of the Communist Party of China (the 「21st CPC National Congress」) is expected to be held in the autumn of next year. He believes that Xi's emphasis on commemorating the centenary of Jiang Zemin's birth, along with praising his choice to firmly uphold the CPC Central Committee, serves to emphasize the political lineage between Xi and Jiang, strengthening recognition of the continuity of his political leadership. At the same time, commemorating Jiang Zemin can also reiterate to Party members the importance of obeying the central leadership and maintaining political loyalty.
